problem: Configuration type and validity are repeated as header badges, while the explorer gives no at-a-glance distinction; success feedback also escaped the previous non-occlusion gate.
scope: Classify every listed config as generic, fragment, valid task, or invalid; decorate the resource tree without relying on color alone; show detailed errors only after opening an invalid file; keep success feedback inline and expiring.
baseline: All tree leaves use the same file icon and muted text; type badges consume editor-header space; list API returns paths only; a fixed success notice can cover controls.
benchmarks: VS Code list.errorForeground and FileDecoration tooltip/color contract
GitHub Primer TreeView leading/trailing visual accessibility contract
Material Design state indicators with redundant visual cues
Community reports that full red filenames can create excessive noise
advantages: Layered config diagnosis already has four required outcomes
Tree nodes already have a stable data-file identity
Opened invalid files already expose diagnostic errors inline
disadvantages: The list endpoint does not expose diagnosis
The previous overlay check did not reject fixed non-interactive notices
limitations: Classification is refreshed when the file list reloads
Syntax-invalid files can only provide parse errors, not field diagnosis
Color names are theme tokens rather than user-customizable settings
defects: State is redundantly rendered in the editor header
Success feedback can occlude the workbench
bottlenecks: Per-file diagnosis must remain isolated so one broken file does not break the list
Selected-row styling must preserve state meaning
Tree virtualisation requires metadata in node data

metrics.name: explorer_classification_coverage
metrics.measurement: generic, fragment, valid task and invalid fixtures expose a state

metrics.name: non_color_state_coverage
metrics.measurement: each file state has an accessible text label and distinct icon shape

metrics.name: invalid_open_error_visibility
metrics.measurement: opened invalid fixture renders an inline alert with concrete errors

metrics.name: success_notice_occlusion
metrics.measurement: success notice position is static and disappears within five seconds

hypotheses: A compact icon plus restrained semantic color and accessible state text is faster to scan than header badges
Returning diagnosis beside paths lets the tree update atomically
Keeping error detail in the opened workbench avoids turning the tree into an error report
An inline auto-expiring success status cannot cover controls
allowed_variables: resource tree node metadata and icons

stages.output: accessible compact tree decorations and inline opened-file errors
quality records, reusable rule writeback and current demo

hard_gates: all four file classifications appear in the explorer
a malformed file cannot break explorer listing
selected and dark-theme rows preserve readable state
invalid details appear only in the opened workbench
validity/type badges are absent from the editor header
success notice never uses fixed or absolute positioning and expires
axe serious and critical violations remain zero
failure_fixtures: invalid task shown with valid icon
syntax-invalid YAML aborts the complete listing
success_fixtures: opened invalid task with inline errors
rollback: Restore path-only list projection and uniform file icon; preserve user configuration files and task history.

iteration_budget.review_trigger: one hard gate failure or a state not distinguishable without color

stop_conditions: all success, failure and fault fixtures are classified
Edge verifies tree semantics and opened error detail
full Python, Edge, quality and Ubuntu gates pass
current demo reloads the accepted assets

promotion_decision.reason: resource-tree status decoration and non-occluding feedback ownership generalize to operator consoles

writeback: Project paths, screenshots and exact colors stay in project evidence; reusable tree decoration, non-color semantics and feedback placement rules update the local interface reference.
